baseline_models.focus_anchor: فَاتَكُمْ ... فَعَاقَبْتُمْ فَآتُوا ... مِثْلَ مَا أَنفَقُوا
baseline_models.mechanism: A failed-to-recover marital departure leaves an expenditure deficit. The next countervailing outcome is treated as a substitute-bearing turn, and the community converts it into an equal grant; equivalence and protective restraint keep recovery from expanding into punitive excess.

activation_trace.role: Failure of reach supplies the literal loss and makes it an unresolved deficit rather than a completed exchange.
A substitute taken with guarantee turns the countervailing event into a source for making the deficit good.
Giving fixes the direction of value toward the spouse who suffered the loss.
The matching counterpart supplies the exact ceiling and measure of restoration.
Money gone out in expenditure identifies what is replaceable without pricing the departed person.
Protective restraint makes the equal payment a guard against both uncompensated harm and overreach.

changed_reading.before: The verse authorizes retaliation after a wife defects.
changed_reading.after: The verse establishes a communal clearing rule: a cross-border marital loss becomes a bounded financial claim paid from the next countervailing recovery.

baseline_models.focus_anchor: فَعَاقَبْتُمْ following فَاتَكُمْ and preceding فَآتُوا
baseline_models.mechanism: The repeated succession senses of ع ق ب make the payment temporally staged. A departure creates a carried claim; when a later turn or return of resources follows, that successor event discharges the earlier depletion.

activation_trace.role: Going away supplies the completed departure that starts the claim clock.
One thing coming after another supplies the later settlement turn.
Recurrence after recurrence allows the claim to be serviced by a subsequent cycle rather than instant bilateral repayment.
Depletion marks the amount that remains outstanding across turns.
The later giving closes the carried claim.

changed_reading.before: Loss and repayment are a single immediate one-for-one event.
changed_reading.after: The loss becomes a carry-forward claim payable when the community reaches its next resource-bearing turn.

baseline_models.focus_anchor: شَىْءٌ مِّنْ أَزْوَاجِكُمْ paired with مِثْلَ مَا أَنفَقُوا
baseline_models.mechanism: The indefinite reportable 'thing' packages a marital rupture as an administrable case, but the remedy measures only prior expenditure. The spouse is the person whose departure occasions the claim, while money, not the person, is made fungible.

activation_trace.role: A knowable, reportable thing supplies the legal case-unit created by the rupture.
The marriage partner anchors the case in an actual spousal bond rather than a generic asset class.
Similarity applies to the measured expenditure, separating financial equivalence from equivalence between persons.
Outgoing money supplies the sole explicit valuation base.

changed_reading.before: A wife is treated as lost property whose value must be replaced.
changed_reading.after: A spouse remains nonfungible; what the rule quantifies and restores is the financial consequence of a broken marriage.

baseline_models.mechanism: The clause opens a punitive semantic possibility and immediately redirects its yield into giving. Exact equivalence and self-protection domesticate retaliation: recovered power repairs the harmed member instead of licensing an enlarging counter-harm.

activation_trace.role: Punishment after wrongdoing supplies the live retaliatory edge of the clause.
The immediate command to give redirects the result of that punitive turn toward restitution.
A matching counterpart prevents the redirected recovery from exceeding the original outlay.
Putting oneself within protection frames restraint itself as communal self-preservation.
Heart-settling trust ties the restrained response to the community's professed belief.

changed_reading.before: A successful counterstroke authorizes punishment of the opposing side.
changed_reading.after: The counterstroke is ethically rerouted: its actionable outcome is an exact restorative payment to the person left short.

context_deltas.mechanism: The opening context makes cross-boundary attachment a site of secrecy and contrasts what is hidden with what is declared. Activated against the concealed-exit branch of ن ف ق, the exact payout in 60:11 reads as visibility repair: an opaque relational and monetary exit is converted into a public, auditable claim.

activation_trace.role: Keeping something inwardly hidden supplies the opacity surrounding a cross-boundary attachment.
Concealment intensifies the problem of an event whose social and financial consequences are not yet legible.
Manifest disclosure supplies the opposite pole toward which a measured settlement moves the loss.
An entrance shown while an exit is hidden makes expenditure an image of value disappearing through an opaque outlet.
The exact counterpart makes the formerly opaque loss publicly reckonable.

structural_cues: 60:1 explicitly juxtaposes concealed and declared conduct around attachment across the hostile boundary; 60:11 names an exact payable amount.
context_deltas.reader_inference: The packet supplies hidden/open polarity and a concealed-exit image for expenditure; I infer that quantified settlement restores public legibility. A live alternative is that 60:1 concerns divine knowledge only and contributes no accounting function.

changed_reading.before: The equivalent payment merely replaces private expenditure.
changed_reading.after: The payment also turns an opaque cross-boundary loss into a declared communal ledger entry that can be settled without rumor or hidden reprisal.

context_deltas.mechanism: Earlier hostile power is pictured as hands extended in harm. In the focus ayah, retaliatory capacity is followed not by an answering harmful hand but by an order to give an equivalent; the same field of operative power is redirected from injury to repair.

activation_trace.role: Extending and releasing the hand makes hostile action an outward use of capacity.
The hand as power supplies the capacity that could be mirrored in retaliation.
Active harm identifies the destructive direction that the focus command refuses to reproduce.
Punitive response keeps reciprocal harm genuinely available at the semantic threshold.
Giving reverses the direction of operative power from striking outward to restoring inward.

structural_cues: 60:2 coordinates extended hands and tongues with harm, while 60:11 coordinates the countervailing turn with an immediate command to give.
context_deltas.reader_inference: The packet supplies hostile embodied capacity and the focus supplies punitive potential followed by giving; I infer a deliberate redirection of power. The alternative is that the two hand-fields are merely sequentially unrelated.

changed_reading.before: The community answers the enemy's harmful reach with its own successful reach.
changed_reading.after: The community's recovered reach is made reparative: victory's hand must fund the harmed insider rather than imitate the hostile hand.

context_deltas.mechanism: The same broad 'thing' language occurs near an explicit negation of possession or disposal. That recurrence sharpens the focus distinction between person and claim: communal authority can restore a measured outlay, but it cannot own, retrieve, or substitute for the departing spouse.

activation_trace.role: Possession and power of disposal are explicitly negated nearby, checking a proprietary reading of the focus loss.
The repeated general reportable 'thing' sits under that negated possession and activates a nonproprietary scope.
In the focus, the same general noun packages the rupture as a cognizable case.
The actual marriage relation keeps the case personal even while its remedy is financial.
Outgoing money, not the spouse, remains the explicit object of equivalence.

structural_cues: In 60:4, 'I possess nothing for you' negates disposal over a شَيْء; in 60:11, the remedy is syntactically fixed to what was spent.
context_deltas.reader_inference: The packet supplies repeated ش ي ء, negated possession, and a monetary remedy; I infer that the focus noun denotes a claim-event rather than chattel. The live alternative is ordinary partitive idiom with no anti-proprietary emphasis.

changed_reading.before: The phrase 'anything of your wives' objectifies a departing woman as communal property.
changed_reading.after: The phrase makes the rupture administrable while denying the community a proprietary remedy: it can settle expenditure, not possess or reclaim the person.

context_deltas.mechanism: The announced possibility that enmity may become affection gives exact compensation a future-facing function. Closing the residual claim without excess prevents a marital-border loss from hardening into an indefinitely inherited feud.

activation_trace.role: Actual enmity supplies the hostile relation within which the focus loss occurs.
Possible affection supplies a reversible future for a relation now marked by hostility.
The consequence of the loss is made finite rather than allowed to perpetuate itself.
Exact matching closes the debt without producing a fresh surplus grievance.

structural_cues: 60:7 places possible future affection precisely between parties previously in enmity; 60:11 closes a concrete loss with a finite equivalent.
context_deltas.reader_inference: The packet supplies reversible enmity and a bounded settlement; I infer that debt closure preserves room for reconciliation. Affection could instead arise independently of this financial rule, so the enabling arrow remains abductive.

changed_reading.before: Compensation only looks backward to cancel a past loss.
changed_reading.after: Compensation also protects a possible shared future by ending the claim without making hostility economically self-renewing.

context_deltas.mechanism: The context distinguishes peaceful outsiders from fighters and expellers, commands equity, and names withholding a right as injustice. Those cues prevent 'to the disbelievers' from licensing category-wide confiscation; the focus recovery is bounded by the particular expenditure claim and its exact equivalent.

activation_trace.role: Equity toward noncombatants supplies the governing norm across the group boundary.
A just share or division gives the focus equivalent the character of an allocated due.
Withholding and confining a right names the wrong that exact compensation repairs without creating another.
The counterpart fixes recovery to the claimant's actual outlay.
Protective restraint keeps a valid recovery claim from turning into indiscriminate seizure.

structural_cues: 60:8-9 sort outsiders by fighting and expulsion rather than by one undifferentiated label; 60:11 specifies a claimant and an amount.
context_deltas.reader_inference: The packet supplies a behavioral distinction, equity, and withheld-right imagery; I infer that the focus remedy is conduct-bounded restitution, not collective punishment. An alternative is that the distinction governs alliance only while compensation follows a separate wartime rule.

changed_reading.before: Once a spouse reaches the disbelieving side, any opposing property may be taken in categorical reprisal.
changed_reading.after: The hostile boundary does not suspend equity: recovery is a particular claimant's measured due, constrained against both underpayment and collective overreach.

context_deltas.mechanism: The preceding rule verifies a migrant's status, forbids forced return, recognizes the old bond as no longer operative, and establishes reciprocal reimbursement requests. The focus ayah then reads as the residual-case handler: when the opposite side does not return an expenditure claim, the next resource-bearing turn substitutes for that failed bilateral refund under communal adjudication.

activation_trace.role: Separation and departure establish a real migration rather than a spouse being physically recoverable as property.
Testing that reveals the heart supplies a status-verification gate before the financial unwind.
Untying a knot images the dissolution of the former marital attachment once return is barred.
Repeated giving supplies both refund and new marital payment as directional transfers rather than ownership of women.
Repeated expenditure defines the bilateral monetary claims on both sides.
A fastening bond supplies the attachment that the rule says not to keep holding.
Mutual requesting supplies the ordinary bilateral reimbursement channel whose failure leaves the focus case.
Judgment between parties frames the transfers as adjudicated settlement rather than opportunistic taking.
A substitute backed by guarantee supplies the fallback payer when direct reciprocity fails.
The exact counterpart preserves the prior rule's claim amount in the fallback path.

structural_cues: 60:10 repeatedly pairs giving, spending, and mutual asking before 60:11 opens with the conditional failure form وَإِن فَاتَكُمْ.
The focus command pays those whose spouses went away, preserving the claimant and amount established by the preceding bilateral rule.
context_deltas.reader_inference: The packet supplies status verification, dissolved bonds, reciprocal claims, adjudication, and then a failed-to-recover condition; I infer an exception-handler arrow from failed direct refund to pooled substitution. A live alternative is that فَعَاقَبْتُمْ refers narrowly to later spoils without implying a standing communal pool.

changed_reading.before: 60:11 is an isolated command to retaliate after a separate marital defection.
changed_reading.after: 60:11 is the fallback branch of 60:10's bilateral settlement protocol: an unpaid refund claim is carried into the next recovery and paid by substitution.

context_deltas.mechanism: The following verse presents women as direct covenanting agents whose pledge is accepted within a recognized-good limit. That agency feeds back into 60:11: departure changes allegiance and dissolves a contract, while equivalent reimbursement settles the abandoned spouse's outlay without buying, returning, or valuing the woman.

activation_trace.role: A pledge of allegiance makes the women active covenant-makers rather than passive objects transferred between groups.
Recognized good constrains the accepted pledge and supplies a normative limit on communal authority.
The woman's going remains an action with a completed direction, not an asset's passive disappearance.
The former marital relation explains the financial residue without exhausting the woman's new covenantal identity.
Only expenditure is restored, leaving allegiance and personhood outside the compensation measure.

structural_cues: 60:12 has the women themselves initiate and enter the pledge; 60:11 directs payment to the spouses left behind rather than directing return of the women.
context_deltas.reader_inference: The packet supplies direct female covenanting agency and a monetary-only remedy; I infer that the focus treats migration as an agentive change with contractual residue. The alternative is that 60:12 begins a distinct procedure and does not color the prior noun phrase.

changed_reading.before: The community compensates for women who have been transferred to another side.
changed_reading.after: Women change covenantal location as agents; the community settles the old marriage's financial residue while leaving their movement irreversible by property logic.

surprising_valid_outliers.containment: This is surprising because it composes spatial and hydraulic branch images rather than translating any one word that way. It remains focus-anchored in the gap, pair, passage, and giving roots, and should be rendered only as a material analogy for the settlement mechanism, not as the lexical sense of the ayah.

activation_trace.role: A gap between two things images the opening left by a broken pair.
Two joined counterparts supply the pair whose rupture creates the gap.
A passage with an outlet makes spent value something that can be routed rather than simply vanish.
A directed watercourse supplies the analogy for channeling replacement value toward the stranded side.

changed_reading.before: Reimbursement statically fills a monetary deficit.
changed_reading.after: The community acts like a channel around a rupture, rerouting value through the gap left by a broken pair so the loss does not pool at one abandoned spouse.

surprising_valid_outliers.containment: This is surprising because it activates a form-distant punitive branch of م ث ل beside the surface sense of equivalence. The contrast remains anchored in the focus root and its explicit punishment-giving sequence, but downstream prose must present it as an intraradical brake on excess, never as a claim that مِثْل means mutilation here.

activation_trace.role: Punishment makes retaliatory escalation a live neighboring mechanism.
Exemplary mutilation supplies the root's disturbing punitive edge against which the surface equivalence can be heard.
The actual matching counterpart selects measured restoration over punitive disfigurement.
Giving fixes the chosen action as transfer to the harmed party rather than bodily counter-harm.
Protective restraint contains the punitive possibility at the exact-equivalence boundary.

changed_reading.before: The word 'equivalent' is only an arithmetic instruction.
changed_reading.after: Exact equivalence also functions as an anti-escalation choice at the semantic edge of exemplary punishment: restore the outlay, do not mark bodies or multiply harm.

surprising_valid_outliers.containment: This is surprising because it lets the later grave-and-despair imagery reactivate the sudden-death branch of ف و ت. It remains anchored in the focus's loss, departure, succession, and payment sequence, but should be qualified as a social analogy: the verse does not call migration death or promise restoration of the marriage.

activation_trace.role: Sudden loss that forecloses intended action supplies a death-like image of irreversible rupture.
Completed departure anchors the analogy in an actual going-away event.
Hope cut off supplies the temptation to treat the rupture as extinguishing every remaining claim.
Burial and concealment make claim-extinction imaginable as a social death.
A successor event keeps a consequence of the ended relation socially alive.
Payment materializes that surviving claim without reversing the departure.

changed_reading.before: An irreversible departure extinguishes the abandoned spouse's relation and every consequence with it.
changed_reading.after: The marriage may end, but the community refuses a financial civil death: the stranded claim remains alive long enough to pass into a successor payment.

strongest_changes: The ع ق ب branches allow 60:11 to coexist as retaliation, successor turn, and substitute guarantee, with the syntax redirecting all three toward exact restorative payment.
60:10 makes the focus ayah legible as a fallback path for a failed bilateral refund rather than an isolated reprisal rule.
The repeated ش ي ء under negated possession in 60:4 and direct female covenanting in 60:12 separate the woman's agency from the strictly financial claim.
The equity and future-affection cues of 60:7-9 make settlement both bounded against collective overreach and capable of preserving reconciliation.
summary.what_was_special: The focus roots formed unusually productive near-collisions: punishment versus succession and guarantee in ع ق ب, equivalence versus exemplary mutilation in م ث ل, and spent money versus a concealed or traversable exit in ن ف ق. These support administrative, temporal, ethical, and material readings at once without requiring one to cancel the others.
remaining_uncertainties: The exact historical referent of فَعَاقَبْتُمْ remains open among retaliation, acquisition of spoils, and a later reciprocal turn.
The fallback-pool mechanism is strongly induced by 60:10-11 but the packet does not explicitly identify the source or administrator of the replacement funds.
The nonproprietary reading of شَيْءٌ is contextually strengthened but is not a proof that the partitive wording itself carries an anti-objectification sense.

The visibility-repair, reconciliation-enabling, hydraulic, anti-mutilatory, and civil-death models are abductive activations and should remain qualified rather than harmonized into the core legal reading.
